..
Weak trade wind showers are making their way over the Marianas this
afternoon. Moisture is expected to stay high enough for this pattern
to continue for much of the week. A brief island induced 
thunderstorm was visible off the coast of Guam today, but winds are 
expected to continue to keep any isolated thunderstorms off the coast
again tomorrow. Decreasing wind shear will likely prevent any 
thunderstorm development on Tuesday with island effect showers
remaining a possibility with the lighter winds. The location of a
pocket of drier air moving into the region beginning Tuesday could
limit the development of these showers, so keeping chances as
isolated for now.

Marine...
Models, coastal buoys, SOFAR buoys, and spotter observations indicate
that surf is high enough to induce a moderate risk of rip currents
along north, east, and west facing reefs tonight through at least
Monday night. Combined seas of 4 to 5 foot will remain through at
least Monday night before starting to slowly decrease. The dominant
swells are the easterly trade wind swell and the westerly swell from
Typhoon Jangmi over the Philippine Sea. Gentle to moderate east winds
are expected to decrease Tuesday.

Eastern Micronesia...
Latest satellite imagery shows mostly isolated showers across the
region north of 5N, with low-end scattered showers seen over Kosrae.
Altimetry shows seas of 4 to 5 feet for Pohnpei and Kosrae, and 4 to
5 feet for Majuro.

The region is a bit drier today than was previously expected. Why?
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) dropped much farther south, faster 
than expected. This has resulted in a fairly dry pattern across the 
region. Only Kosrae is seeing any real shower activity, with only 
low-end scattered showers expected through tonight. Model guidance is
trying to rush the NET back to the north a bit faster than is 
likely, so the dry pattern looks to continue through Tuesday. Then 
the NET is expected to be far enough north to bring in increased 
showers to all three forecast points. However, POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) will be the lowest at Majuro, only reaching 30 percent
for a short time Tuesday night before again drying out. Pohnpei and 
Kosrae will see POPs bouncing around between 20 and 40 percent 
through the end of the week as the NET meanders around the area. 

For the marine forecast, no big changes were made. Overall light to 
occasionally gentle winds are expected across the region, with seas 
of 3 to 5 feet for Pohnpei and Kosrae dropping slightly to between 2 
and 4 feet Monday. Majuro seas will drop from 4 to 5 feet to 3 to 4 
feet around midweek.

Western Micronesia...
To the distant northwest, TY Jangmi continues to steer monsoon
southwesterly winds across the Phillipines, with only a few clusters
of showers and thunderstorms passing west and northwest of Palau and
Yap. A ridge of high pressure is breaking up this pattern, bringing a
lull in showers this evening, however, a broad but weak disturbance 
in the near-equatorial trough (NET) moves from southern Chuuk State 
into southeastern Yap State overnight. The western portion of the NET
begins to push into far western Micronesia, bringing an uptick in 
showers overnight and Monday for Yap and Palau. Latest model guidance
continues to depict convection loosely organized around the NET 
which looks to bring periods of scattered showers for Yap and Palau 
this week. At Chuuk, trade-wind convergence northeast of the NET 
disturbance looks to rebuild showers over the area late tonight. 
Besides subtle shifts in the NET, this pattern looks to remain across
central Micronesia this week, maintaining periods of scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms for Chuuk through at least Friday.

Northwest swell from distant TY Jangmi and southwest monsoon swell 
are producing 5 to 7 foot seas at Yap and Palau. Meanwhile, northeast
trade-wind swell and light west swell are producing seas of 4 to 5 
feet at Chuuk. As northwest and west-southwest swells gradually 
diminish, combined seas are expected to subside to 3 to 4 feet by 
Tuesday night. Light to gentle winds at Yap and Palau and gentle to 
moderate winds at Chuuk, further diminish to light and variable by 
Monday night.
